title: Fppf restriction preserves a groupoid quotient and reflects relation monicity
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid scheme over $S$ [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Let $q:U'\to U$ be a surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally finitely presented morphism [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], so that $\{q\}$ is an fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site]. Form the restriction $R'=U'\times_{q,U,s}R\times_{t,U,q}U'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with its groupoid structure on $U'$. If $(s',t'):R'\to U'\times_SU'$ is a monomorphism, then $(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ is a monomorphism. Here monomorphism means injectivity on sections over every test $S$-scheme; consequently the two groupoids in this case are equivalence relations. Without any monicity assumption, write $U/R$ and $U'/R'$ for the fppf sheafifications [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaves of isomorphism classes of their test-scheme groupoids. The canonical morphism $U'/R'\longrightarrow U/R$ induced by $q$ is an isomorphism of fppf sheaves. No separatedness, finiteness, or affineness hypothesis on $U,R,q$ is imposed beyond the stated fppf covering condition. All schemes and fibre products are in the chosen site bound.

source.place: Tag 02VH (lemma-quotient-groupoid-restrict), fppf covering case. Reflection of monicity is descent.tex Tag 02YK (lemma-descending-property-monomorphism), applied to (s,t) after the product fppf covering U-prime x_S U-prime -> U x_S U.

proof.text: For each test $S$-scheme $T$, the fibre-product universal property identifies $R'(T)$ with triples $(x,r,y)$ such that $qx=sr$ and $tr=qy$. Give this triple source $x$, target $y$, identity $(x,e(qx),x)$ and inverse $(y,i(r),x)$. Compose $(x,h,y)$ followed by $(y,r,z)$ as $(x,c(r,h),z)$. The endpoint equalities follow from those for $c$; the identity, inverse and associativity laws hold in the middle coordinate by the groupoid laws and in the outer coordinates by equality. All formulas commute with precomposition in $T$, hence define scheme morphisms by the fibre-product universal property applied to the displayed component morphisms. This constructs the restricted groupoid and the forgetful groupoid morphism induced by $q$.

source.place: Tag 02VB (lemma-restrict-groupoid), explicit verification of the omitted construction

proof.text: Assume $(s',t')$ is monic. Given $r_1,r_2:T\to R$ with common source $a:T\to U$ and common target $b:T\to U$, first pull back $q$ along $a$, obtaining an fppf cover $p:T_a\to T$ with a lift $x:T_a\to U'$. Pull back $q$ again along $bp$, obtaining an fppf cover $v:W\to T_a$ with a lift $y:W\to U'$. On $W$ the triples $(xv,r_1pv,y)$ and $(xv,r_2pv,y)$ have the same endpoints, so are equal by the assumed monicity; their middle coordinates give $r_1pv=r_2pv$. Each of $\{v\}$ and $\{p\}$ is fpqc by the fppf-to-fpqc comparison. Uniqueness in representable fpqc descent, first for maps $T_a\to R$ on $v$ and then for maps $T\to R$ on $p$, gives $r_1p=r_2p$ and $r_1=r_2$. Thus $(s,t)$ is monic. In any groupoid, existence of an arrow is reflexive by $e$, symmetric by $i$ and transitive by $c$. Monicity makes this arrow unique, so both groupoids are equivalence relations on every test scheme.

source.place: Tag 02YK (lemma-descending-property-monomorphism), its test-morphism argument; Tag 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms); topologies.tex Tags 021O and 022C

proof.text: Now drop the monicity assumption. Put $P(T)=\pi_0(U(T),R(T))$ and $P'(T)=\pi_0(U'(T),R'(T))$, with restrictions induced by precomposition. Two objects of a groupoid represent the same isomorphism class exactly when an arrow joins them: identity, inverse and composition show arrow existence is already an equivalence relation. The functor in step 1 therefore gives a natural map $v:P'\to P$, $[x]\mapsto[qx]$. If $v_T([x])=v_T([y])$, choose an arrow $r$ from $qx$ to $qy$. The triple $(x,r,y)$ lies in $R'(T)$ and joins $x$ to $y$. Hence $[x]=[y]$, proving $v_T$ injective for every $T$. This uses no uniqueness of arrows.

For $z\in P(T)$ choose a representative $u:T\to U$. The pullback $W=T\times_{u,U,q}U'$ has projections $p:W\to T$ and $x:W\to U'$ with $qx=up$. Its singleton $\{p\}$ is an fppf covering by base change, and $v_W([x])=[up]=z|_W$. Thus $v$ is locally surjective. Every arrow in the sieve generated by $p$ factors through $p$, so pulling back $[x]$ supplies the lifts required in the covering-sieve formulation as well. Sectionwise injectivity from step 3 implies local injectivity, using the maximal covering sieve.

source.place: Tag 02VH (lemma-quotient-groupoid-restrict), covering case; topologies.tex Tag 021O (lemma-fppf), part (3)

proof.text: Apply the set-presheaf local-bijection criterion to $v$ on the big fppf site. The size convention replaces this site by a small skeleton within a universe containing its objects and arrows, as required by that criterion. Steps 3 and 4 verify its two conditions, so $v^\#:P'^\#\to P^\#$ is an isomorphism. By the sheafification universal property this is precisely the canonical morphism $U'/R'\to U/R$ induced by $q$. No argument used separatedness, quasi-compactness, affineness, or a finiteness condition beyond the given fppf cover.
